page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one column on the right, from top to bottom. Marginal notes in a column down the left margin, beside the text lines they stand by. Catchword "de-" at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: Præterquam quod ibi fiscus, non jure fiscins[?] confideretur, verum jure privati, cum altero privato secundum justitiæ leges contendentis.

Quæ hactenus ex jure civili sunt confirmata, eadem & jure feudali probari poterunt. Si enim vasallus domino auxilium præstare tenetur, etiam adversus patrem: quid ni secun-l.fin.tit.dum illa jura patrem necare 28. Hic finiturpoterit. In quem enim arma lex l.2. Bronc.diriguntur, is etiam jure occi-horst.Mi.ditur. Neque videtur illa sen-tentia juris feudalis destitui ratione. Si enim parens injuste scell con-tt.cent.dominum vasalli offendens, i. affert.agat contra jus naturale, con-93. Argum. l.37.in fin. D. de Minor.tra fidem datam, frustra bene-§. fen-tentiæ. de Pace Constant d. §.dict.ficium ullum juris naturalis sperabit, ut qui eo jure sese red-diderit indignum.
Nec obstat quod vasallus, si bellum patriæ & quidem jure tit. Arg. 1.14.D. de leg.inferatur, & patriam defendat,

page.notes: Printed text at the left margin read as: "l.fin.tit.", "28. Hic finitur", "lex l.2. Bronc.", "horst.Mi.", "scell con-tt.cent.", "i. affert.", "93. Argum. l.37.in fin. D. de Minor.", "§. fen-tentiæ. de Pace Constant d. §.dict.", "tit. Arg. 1.14.D. de leg.". Their exact line positions are approximate. Doubtful: "fiscins" in line 2 (probably fiscus, printed as is); "red-diderit" at the line break; "horst" and "scell" (long s/f forms); "1.37.in" versus "l.37.in"; and the marginal "l.fin.tit." which might read "1. fin. tit.". The lines of the margin notes are small and somewhat blurred. The faint marks at the bottom of the page are a digitiser's element and were left out.
